clue.text: Time the smart set went about for somewhere to sleep

parts.note: spring is a time of year, a season

indicators.note: turning about suggests the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: The fashionable crowd have a seasonal outing and need a bed for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went about' rearranges SMART SET into MATTRESS; 'Time' is not T here but a season.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung mattress is the base of a bed, the thing a sleeper lies on.

clue.text: Complaint made by member of air-crew in a drop being aborted

indicators.note: the airman's letters are placed inside the other piece
an aborted drop goes wrong, so its letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: AG is an air gunner, a wartime bomber crew member

explanation.surface: A crew member falls ill after a parachute drop is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being aborted' scrambles the drop's letters; an air gunner was a standard member of a wartime bomber crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Podagra is the medical name for gout in the foot, an ailment.

clue.text: Increase the Japanese might pronounce harsh

indicators.note: the old stereotype that Japanese speakers render L as R points to a spoken substitution

parts.note: inclement weather is harsh and severe

explanation.surface: A remark on how harsh a Japanese speaker's accent might sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on a dated stereotype: INCLEMENT with its L said as R.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an addition or step up in amount.

clue.text: An industrial protest formed from a turn's depression

parts.note: having a go means having a turn
the possessive ending supplies its letter S
a low is a weather depression

explanation.surface: Someone's mood dip is said to have sparked a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-slow is a workers' tactic of deliberately reduced output, short of a strike.

clue.text: Ancient people are about to enquire for North Americans

indicators.note: the old tribe are said to be round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the Alans were a nomadic people of antiquity
to ask is to enquire

explanation.surface: An archaeologist asks about an old tribe living in the New World.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alans were nomads of late antiquity; 'are about' has them enclosing the enquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of the US state in the far north-west of the continent.

clue.text: Something to eat as carried by a child

indicators.note: the little one holds the other piece, so it sits inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A snack being held by a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast is browned bread, a common breakfast food.

clue.text: It enables one to see if you are up on everything

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it
in a down entry, going up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: archaic 'be ye' carries the conditional sense of 'if you are'
all means everything

explanation.surface: Advice that being well informed helps you see things clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: BE YE (as in 'be ye ever so') turned upward gives EYEB, placed on ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe of the organ of sight is what lets a person look.

clue.text: Possibly get a screen part, although only a theatrical worker

indicators.note: a possible version of these words is a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone backstage might build a piece of scenery, though only a humble worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter in a theatre builds the scenery and sets.

clue.text: One who made money in the Wilson days holds the island to be misunderstood

indicators.note: the money-maker holds the island, enclosing it

parts.note: a minter coins money
Is is the abbreviation for island
Harold Wilson preceded Ted Heath as prime minister, so his days were pre-Ted

explanation.surface: A profiteer of the 1960s is accused of misreading an island's situation.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Wilson was UK prime minister before Edward 'Ted' Heath took over in 1970, so his era was pre-Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be misinterpreted is to be wrongly understood.

clue.text: Fingers are caught in remote places

indicators.note: the cricket letter is placed inside the distant lands

parts.note: the Indies, East and West, were faraway lands
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Fingers get trapped in faraway lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Index fingers are pointers; the plural of index can mean these digits.

clue.text: A public walk made by a crippled lawyer

parts.note: lame means crippled
a DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A lame attorney's slow promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a tree-lined promenade, from Spanish.

clue.text: Warm corner of Scots valley in one secluded place

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the valley sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a nook is a quiet recess
a glen is a valley in Scotland

explanation.surface: A cosy spot in a hidden Highland valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The valley goes in just after the N of the secluded place, not between the one and it.
explanation.definitionFit: An inglenook is the seat or recess beside a big open fire.

clue.text: A craft seen in an extra desperate situation

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the run of these words

explanation.surface: A boat glimpsed in dire straits.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled occupation, as a craft is.

clue.text: To tantalise the left is a plant

parts.note: to tease is to tantalise
L is short for left

explanation.surface: Teasing the political left is a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasel is a prickly plant whose heads were used to raise cloth nap.

clue.text: Part of the world for which international organisation will inter alia serve

indicators.note: to inter is to bury, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation

explanation.surface: A region the alliance will serve, among other duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter' looks like part of the Latin phrase 'inter alia', but it is the burial signal acting on 'alia'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the Asian peninsula forming most of Turkey.

clue.text: Car parts pursue petrol without a note

parts.note: to tail is to follow or pursue

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, the fuel wraps round the note

parts.note: gas is American for petrol
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Drivers chase fuel without a receipt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailgates are the hinged rear doors of vehicles.

clue.text: In court since for breaking out

indicators.note: words that break out are smashed apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A prisoner in the dock since an attempted escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic means relating to courts of law.

clue.text: A revolution but possibly not a riot

indicators.note: a possible version of the letters is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: An uprising that may not be a riot at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotation is turning round once, a revolution about an axis.

clue.text: Not having anything lying fallow the picture would be banned

indicators.note: the banned word has the fallow land within it

parts.note: tabu, a variant of taboo, means forbidden
a lea is grassland or untilled land

explanation.surface: Without any fallow land in it, the painting would be censored.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says that the picture without LEA would be TABU; so TABU holds LEA. 'Not' and 'anything' only frame that subtraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque scene or picture.

clue.text: Accident at high point on main road

indicators.note: one piece follows on after the other

parts.note: the M1, written MI, is Britain's first main motorway
Shap is the high summit on the old main road north through Cumbria

explanation.surface: A crash at the summit of a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAP is a notoriously high, exposed pass on the A6 in north-west England; M1 is written MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident.

clue.text: Done how awkwardly as a dance?

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the letters are put clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy performance at a country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance party.

clue.text: By the agency of a style of architecture seen on the right-hand page

parts.note: Perp is short for Perpendicular, an English Gothic style
ro is recto, the right-hand page of a book

explanation.surface: Gothic architecture appears on a book's right-hand page.
explanation.definitionFit: Per pro is Latin for acting on behalf of another, as in signing letters.

clue.text: Fanatical through being born during enemy attack

indicators.note: the birth happens inside the raid, so one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a raid is a hostile attack

explanation.surface: A child turns zealous after being born in an air raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means wildly extreme or zealous.

clue.text: Speak slowly for doctor with sharp implement

parts.note: an awl is a pointed boring tool

explanation.surface: A doctor with a sharp tool speaks unhurriedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To drawl is to talk with lengthened, lazy vowels.

clue.text: Like Laurel and Hardy?

parts.note: laurel is a plant that keeps its leaves all year, and hardy suggests a durable plant; the comic pair also never lose their appeal

explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes leaves that last all year and anything perennially popular.

clue.text: Articles about prohibition among the ancients

parts.note: the is the definite article
bans are prohibitions

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces on prohibition in the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles about prohibition' reads as THE + BANS; the ancients are a particular people of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Thebes were citizens of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Help too may be given in this dangerous place

indicators.note: what may be given is a reworking of these letters

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a hazard may need assistance too.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a deep cave shaft, perilous to explorers.

clue.text: Cheating to get a passage both ways ?

definitions.text: to get a passage both ways
definitions.meaning: a crossing made twice, out and back

explanation.definitionFit: Treachery against an ally, and literally a two-way journey across.
